facts.statement: Xiangyunloong is a genus of massopodan sauropodomorph dinosaur found in the Early Jurassic Fengjiahe Formation of Yunnan, China.
facts.quote: Xiangyunloong (; meaning "auspicious cloud dragon") is a genus of massopodan sauropodomorph dinosaur known from fossils found in the Early Jurassic Fengjiahe Formation of Yunnan, China.

facts.statement: The holotype of Xiangyunloong is a partial skeleton containing vertebrae, rib fragments, chevrons, and parts of the pelvis.
facts.quote: The holotype, YDDY 10001–10041, is a partial skeleton including cervical, dorsal and caudal vertebrae, several dorsal rib fragments, chevrons, an incomplete left ilium, and a right ischium.

facts.statement: The fossils of Xiangyunloong were discovered in the Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Dali Bai Autonomous Prefecture, Yunnan Province, China.

facts.statement: The genus name Xiangyunloong references Xiangyun County, meaning "auspicious clouds".
facts.quote: The generic name, Xiangyunloong, is a reference to Xiangyun (), the county where the holotype was discovered, with a name meaning "auspicious clouds".

facts.statement: The species name fengming references Luming town and the dinosaur-bird connection.
facts.quote: The specific name, fengming, (; literally "phoenix calling"), carries several meanings—it is a reference to Luming (; literally "deer calling"), the town where the holotype was found, as well as a nod to the dinosaur–bird connection.

facts.statement: The holotype of Xiangyunloong is estimated to have been 9 to 10 meters long.
facts.quote: Based on comparisons with the roughly coeval Lishulong and Xingxiulong yueorum, the holotype individual of Xiangyunloong fengming has been estimated to have a body length of 9 - 10 m.

facts.statement: Xiangyunloong belongs to the parent group Massopoda.
Xiangyunloong is classified in the class Saurischia.
Xiangyunloong lived between 201.4 and 174.7 million years ago, from the Hettangian to the Toarcian.
facts.quote: Time range: Hettangian to Toarcian (201.4 to 174.7 million years ago)

facts.statement: Xiangyunloong is distinguished by lateral expansions on cervical neural spines, heightened hyposphene in dorsal vertebrae, and a flaring supracetabular crest on the ilium.
Phylogenetic analysis places Xiangyunloong in an unresolved polytomy with the species of Xingxiulong.
facts.quote: This analysis placed Xiangyunloong in an unresolved polytomy with both species of Xingxiulong.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analysis places Xiangyunloong between Massospondylidae and Sauropodiformes in an unresolved clade with Xingxiulong species.

rejected.statement: Xiangyunloong was described as a new genus and species in 2026.
rejected.quote: It was described as a new genus and species of sauropodomorph dinosaur in 2026.
